chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The waiting period (iddah) of the slave girl is two menstruations. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When she does not menstruate, then [her waiting period is] half the waiting period of the free woman.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a slave girl upon divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific legal ruling for the waiting period (iddah) of a slave woman upon divorce, establishing it as two menstrual cycles. In cases where she is not menstruating, the ruling defaults to half the duration of a free woman's iddah, reflecting the jurisprudential distinction between slave and free status in Shia fiqh. This ruling is derived from the broader Quranic principles governing divorce and waiting periods, applied here with specific nuance for concubines.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Qasim Bin Bureyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A waiting period of the slave girls is of two menstruations’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When she does not happen to be menstruating, so half a waiting period of the free woman’.
